channel.description: Latest articles from The Art Newspaper (theartnewspaper.com)

item.title: Fifty-year restoration of Sainte-Chapelle's monumental stained glass inches closer to completion
item.description: Long-haul conservation project contrasts with the speed of neighbour Notre-Dame’s repair after the 2019 fire

item.title: What happens to the art market when humanity stops mattering?
item.description: In a world now governed by force—as US president Donald Trump and his circle would have it—rather than shared values, art risks being relegated to a power play of ‘proven brands’

item.title: Former Swiss president to head new Nazi loot panel
item.description: The new Commission for Historically Problematic Cultural Heritage—whose remit also includes claims for cultural heritage that changed hands in a colonial context—will issue non-binding recommendations

item.title: Russia's winter bombardment puts strain on Ukrainian museum workers
item.description: Targeted attacks on electric and water supplies amid freezing conditions are further complicating the work of cultural organisations

item.title: UK museum directors join prime minister on diplomatic mission to China
item.description: The visit is intended as a relationship-boosting exercise though the government said the prime minister would also “raise the areas where we disagree with China”

item.title: Art Basel Qatar is the latest addition to a grand national plan
item.description: A drive to develop the commercial sector is the latest push from the government to promote its artists

item.title: Your country needs you(r content): National Gallery of Art in Washington DC launches social media open call
item.description: As part of the US's 250th anniversary celebrations, the museum is looking for 50 digital content creators to make short-form videos in response to its collection

item.title: Sonia Boyce to make new work to mark 200 years of University College London
item.description: The London university has also commissioned works by three artists-in-residence for its bicentenary

item.title: Venice Biennale: South African pavilion scandal, Marian Goodman remembered, Paul Cezanne in Basel—podcast
item.description: We discuss the cancellation of Gabrielle Goliath’s pavilion and the artist’s attempt have the decision overturned, pay tribute to the lauded gallerist Marian Goodman, and hear about Cezanne’s famous ‘The Card Players’

item.title: MFA Boston will lay off 33 employees amid rising deficit and restructuring
item.description: The layoffs amount to a reduction of the museum’s staff by around 6.3% and include 16 unionised workers
